newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati questioned over meeting.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati questioned over meeting.

text.p: Ousted Indonesian minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri was questioned by police for five hours on Thursday over the organisation of a political rally at her home last month and a speech she delivered.

Police have said the meeting was illegal because Megawati, who was ousted as leader of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) by a government-backed rival last year, had not notified the authorities about it.
One of her lawyers, Erick Paat, told reporters after Megawati emerged tight-lipped from the South Jakarta Police Headquarters that she would be questioned again on March 5.

Around 1,000 supporters watched by more than 100 riot police, many armed with assault rifles, blocked the street outside the police building after Megawati entered. They later dispersed without incident.

Lawyers for Megawati also said they had lodged a new law suit with the Jakarta State Administrative Court on Thursday, asking that the police summonses for both Megawati and her husband Taufik Kiemas be overturned as they were not properly constituted.

The respondents in the suit are Indonesian President Suharto, State Secretary Murdiono, Attorney-General Singgih and the South Jakarta police chief. Under Indonesian law, the president must give police permission to question a member of parliament.

Megawati is still a member of parliament, although her name has not been accepted to stand in the next general elections on May 29 following her ouster as leader of the PDI, one of only three parties permitted to contest the polls.
